content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Ask How much is or are and state a simple price. Model: “How much are the socks? They are eight pounds.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use asking the price clearly and politely. One useful response is: “How much are the socks? They are eight pounds.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where asking the price is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.

listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about asking the price.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about asking the price. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: How much are the socks?
listening.transcript: How much is this hat? It is five pounds. How much are these socks? They are three pounds.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.

pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Use is for one item and are for more than one item. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Use is for one item and are for more than one item.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about asking the price.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using asking the price; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise asking the price?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: How much are the socks? They are eight pounds.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about asking the price with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about asking the price. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: How much are the socks? They are eight pounds. Submit your draft first.
